title.narrative: Working with Men to Increase Security and Stabilization in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri provinces

description.narrative: The goal of the proposed intervention is to achieve sustainable, gender-equitable peace at all levels of society in provinces of South Kivu, North Kivu and Ituri in eastern DRC by: 1. The overall goal of LPI is to reduce level of violence and build trust in the community by working with men through psychosocial support programs that will help them to end violence and adopt norms and values that support gender equality at all levels; 2. Promoting women socio-economic empowerment with positive support of husbands through an adaptation of the Living Peace methodology, (Journeys of Transformation). LPI is partnering with a local organization (Centre Rafiki) to implement Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) for spouses of former military and police men LP psychosocial group beneficiaries for women socio-economic empowerment. LPI will train the local partner in the application of Journeys of Transformation module to engage men as allies of women in economic empowerment.

The intervention seeks to achieve its goal by pursuing following objectives at five different levels: 1. Individual Level: Men and women (spouses), healed of severe mental health and psychosocial problems, adopted positive non-violent coping strategies and experience greater personal efficacy to build meaningful relations with self and others. 2. Family Level: Reduced violence at home and restored peaceful partner relations create a safe and healthy environment for women, men and children. Reduction of violence use by men against their partners and children and increase gender equitable behaviors in the household create a safer environment for all members of the family. 3. Community Level: Restored community-based social support systems increase social cohesion between families, individuals and community structures resulting in higher levels of inclusion, and solidarity between community members. 4. Society Level: Congolese civil society organizations and public institutions of Police, Army and Health Care and religious leaders institutionalized the Living Peace approach in their services to adequately address the consequences of SGBV, promote positive masculinity and prevent (mainly) men getting involved in conflicts and/or (re)join armed groups. 5. Women Social and Economic Empowerment: Women, partners of male participants in Living Peace groups, enjoy greater social and economic autonomy with positive support of husbands that participated in Living Peace groups.

The intervention targets the categories below: 1. Husband’s of women survivors of SGBV. 2. Military Men and Police Men (PNC) 4. Civilian Men living in Community in high risk zones 5. Ex-combatant and ex child soldiers living in Community in high risk zones 6. Spouses of military men and policemen participating into the LP program

recipient-country.narrative: The activity is implemented in Noth-Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri provinces. In North Kivu Province the project is being implemented in 6 health zones notably Goma, Karisimbi, Nyiragongo, Kirotche, Masisi and Mweso. In south Kivu Province, The project is being implemented in 4 Health zones notably Bagira, Ibanda, Nyantende and Lemera. In Ituri province, the project is being implemented in 2 Health zones notably Bunia and Nizi.

Objective 2: Family Level: Reduced Violence at Home and Restored Peaceful Partner relations in the family

description.narrative: At family level, the LP program aims at reducing violence at home and restore peaceful partner relations in the family. At this level, the men’s psychosocial support groups and the inclusion of women through weekly homework tasks and in shared sessions with men both work to reduce the use of violence by men against their partners and children, increase relationship quality, and increase gender equitable behaviors in the household, thus creating a safer and more equal environment for all members of the family.

title.narrative: Output Indicator 2.1. Number of Targeted men actively participate in gender and violence components of the psychosocial support group.

description.narrative: According to LP Psychosocial support manual, gender and violence components covers from session 5 up to session 8. During these sessions, men participants discuss and share experiences about power and interpersonal relations, sex and sexuality, breaking the cycle of violence and Responsible man, husband and father. Discussions within this component pursuit the following main goals: 1.To help every participant to challenge the way he uses his power in order to be aware of the consequences of power inequalities in relationships to improve their interpersonal relationship,. 2. Enable participants to challenging their perceptions of sex and sexuality in order to recognize the importance of acceptance and mutual respect in sexual relationships. 3. Encourage participants to reflect on personal experiences of violence as an author, witness and/or victim within their families in order to identify factors that contribute to the use of violence against their partners and effective ways to prevent the escalation of violence. 4. Allow participants to discuss the meaning of responsibility as a man, husband and father, the impact of negative perceptions of responsibility on their lives and those of their families in order to contribute to their modification, the creation of peace and stability within their families and the community.

title.narrative: Outcome 2.1.2: Reports (from men and women participants) of improved communication in partner relationship

description.narrative: Communication is an important competence in family relations and conflict management. It is through communication that men and women can listen and identify everyone needs triggers of conflicts and positive ways of managing them

comment.narrative: For the Year 2020-2021, the number of men living in harmony with their wives increased from 29.8% at pre-intervention to 83.9 % at post intervention. The percentage of men who use dialogue to find solutions to family problems increased from 26.5% to 76.9%. The percentage of men who dialogue with their wives to get mutual consent for sexual intercourse increased from 28.5% to 85.3 %. The percentage of men who dialogue with their wives about children education increased from 37% to 83.1%.

For the first round of LP psychosocial support group for the year 2021-2022, the percentage of men who use dialogue to find solutions to family problems increased from 23.5% to 74.6%. The percentage of men who dialogue with their wives to get mutual consent for sexual intercourse increased from 32.5% to 86.1 %. The percentage of men who dialogue with their wives about children education increased from 34.6% to 82.8%.

The pre and post self-administered questionnaire data showed a significant increase in terms of involving wife in resolving family problems as well as decision making, Before the LP intervention only 25% of LP participants agreed that they could involved their wife in solving family problems, 29.1% said they used to talk to their wife about sexual relationship while only 29.2% of them were able to plan together with their wife about family expenses. After joining LP project 64.4% of male participants argued they are now able to involve their wife to solve family problems and 70.1% of them start talking to their wife about their sexual relationship while 80.6% start planning with their wife on their expenses.

description.narrative: LP psychosocial support program includes family-focused shared sessions during which targeted men and their spouses meet to discuss how their can put their effort together to end the cycle of violence in their families and communities. Shared sessions reinforce more gender equitable attitudes and behaviors, improve communication in partner relationship and reduce men’s use of physical, sexual, psychological and economic, violence against women & violence against children. Shared sessions are 9th entitled family sharing, 11th entitled new rules, attitudes and habits at home, 12th session entitled Barriers and opportunities for change, 13th session entitled security networks and neighbors' groups and the 15th session entitled community celebration.

title.narrative: Outcome Indicator 2.1.1: Reports (from men and women participants including in polygamous relations) of more gender equitable attitudes and full caregiving responsibilities for their respective spouses and children in the households of participating men.

description.narrative: Prevalence of traditional gender attitudes predicted rates of violence against women, specifically sexual assault and domestic violence. In families with more traditional gender attitudes, there were substantial increases in sexual and physical violence inflicted upon women by men. LP approaches are transformative in such a way it actively seeks to examine, challenge and modify rigid gender norms and power imbalances. It encourage critical awareness; question the cost of harmful and inequitable gender norms and help the participant to internalize the the benefits of changing them; empowering women/girls and engage boys and men in the areas of gender equality, violence prevention, and sexual and reproductive health.

comment.narrative: Before LP intervention husbands had never considering them as a person or human being, some time because of not earning any money or because of coming from a different ethnic group. only 13.7% of participating men were able to revealed that they can cook and clean t home while only 18.1% of men said they able to wash and feed their own children. After joining the LP psychosocial support group session, the number of men who developed gender equitable attitudes and supporting their spouses to perform household activities have considerably increased, 43.8% of participating men are now able to help their spouse to cook and clean their house while 40.3% said they are now loving to take care on housework and childcare responsibilities like washing and feeding their kids.

Men participants in LP psychosocial support groups acquired new gender attitudes to support equality between men and women and engagement in the prevention of SVBG. The percentage of men who believe that changing diapers, washing and feeding children are tasks of women decreased from 61.2% to 12.1%. The percentage of men who believe that a woman who does not dress in a decent manner is at risk of being raped decreased from 66.8% to 18.7%. The percentage of men who believe that there are times when women deserve to be beaten decreased from 58.6% to 5.8%. The percentage of men who was totally agreed that a woman must tolerate violence to keep her family together decreased from 78.9% to 16.4%.

Participation in LP psychosocial support group has been revealed to be associated with reduction of harmful gender attitudes which support inequality and justify violent behaviors of men and the adoption of positive attitudes which support equality between men and women. The comparison of results from pre-post intervention questionnaire show that men participants in LP psychosocial support groups acquired new gender attitudes to support equality between men and women and engagement in the prevention of SVBG. The percentage of men who believe that changing diapers, washing and feeding children are tasks of women decreased from 54.2% to 8.9%. The percentage of men who believe that a woman who does not dress in a decent manner is at risk of being raped decreased from 63.1% to 14.7%. The percentage of men who believe that there are times when women deserve to be beaten decreased from 51.6% to 6.8%. It is these changes in gender attitudes and the improvement of mental health conditions which can explain new behaviors among LP group participants.

description.narrative: LPI is working with ex-combatants and ex-child soldiers in Kirotche and Mweso health zones to help them to address a range of psychosocial challenges during their transition to civilian life in order to increase their prospects for successful reintegration. This includes the healing of individual and social trauma; reduce the effects of stigma and exclusion in order to create a space that facilitates the process of reconciliation between ex-combatants, their families and communities. description.narrative:
Living Peace Methodology is a combination of psychosocial support and gender transformative techniques to help men in post-conflict settings to address the personal effects of trauma related to war and violence. The methodology integrated results of research on gender relations in DRC (IMAGES 2012) and tested methodologies of behavior changes (Manual WB 2012). title.narrative: Outcome Indicator 1.4.1: Reports (from men and women participants) of improved trust and confidence in others, stronger social cohesion in the community and a restored sense of belongingness among participating men

description.narrative: Trust, confidence in others, social cohesion and sense of belongingness are key elements for a successful family and social life. The term ‘social cohesion’ is used to describe the bonds that bring people together. Triggers for such bonds can include eating meals and playing games or doing activities with other people, collective/shared experiences. A cohesive community is one where strong bonds and relationships are developed between people of different backgrounds and circumstances. ‘Sense of belonging’ or ‘community’ has been defined as individuals’ sense of being accepted, valued, included, and encouraged by others in the community setting and of feeling oneself to be an important part of the life and activity of the community. Failure to feel a sense of belonging may lead to feelings of social isolation, alienation, and loneliness. The More the individual experience a sense of belonging in the community the more are motivated, engaged in community activities, and more dedicated to the community. Individual who feel they belong to the community also report greater enjoyment, enthusiasm, happiness, interest, and more confidence in engaging community activities, whereas those who feel isolated report greater anxiety, boredom, frustration, and sadness which directly and negatively affects social life.

description.narrative: VSLAs are implemented in tree main phases. The Preparatory phase, which consists of providing general information to local leaders and prospective VSLA members . It then continues to meetings, in which the Association learns to manage social fund, share-purchase/savings and loan transactions. And the development and maturity phase during which the field officer ensures through evaluations and verification that the association can run successfully for long periods without supervision or support to graduate the Association to full independence. During the VSLA cycle (9-12 months), VSLA Members learn how to create and make functioning VSLAs in their community with the full support of trained field Agents.
